arxiv-1910-04860.title: Generative One-Shot Face Recognition
arxiv-1910-04860.creator: Zhengming Ding, Yandong Guo, Lei Zhang, and Yun Fu
arxiv-1910-04860.description: Abstract One-shot face recognition measures the ability to identify persons with only seeing them at one glance, and is a hallmark of human visual intelligence. It is challenging for conventional machine learning approaches to mimic this way, since limited data are hard to effectively represent the data variance.

arxiv-2212-10713.title: Quantum vs classical Markov chains; Exactly solvable examples
arxiv-2212-10713.description: Abstract A coinless quantisation procedure of general reversible Markov chains on graphs is presented. A quantum Hamiltonian ℋ \mathcal{H} is obtained by a similarity transformation of the fundamental transition probability matrix K K in terms of the square root of the reversible distribution.

arxiv-2312-06614.title: AttenScribble: Attentive Similarity Learning for Scribble-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
arxiv-2312-06614.creator: Mu Tian, Qinzhu Yang, Yi Gao
arxiv-2312-06614.description: Abstract The success of deep networks in medical image segmentation relies heavily on massive labeled training data. However, acquiring dense annotations is a time-consuming process. Weakly-supervised methods normally employ less expensive forms of supervision, among which scribbles started to gain popularity lately thanks to its flexibility.

arxiv-2401-11060.title: A Molev-Sagan type formula for double Schubert polynomials
arxiv-2401-11060.creator: Matthew J. Samuel
arxiv-2401-11060.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Matthew J. Samuel. We give a Molev-Sagan type formula for computing the product 𝔖 u ⁡ ( x ; y ) ​ 𝔖 v ⁡ ( x ; z ) \sch_{u}(x;y)\sch_{v}(x;z) of two double Schubert polynomials in different sets of coefficient variables where the descents of u u and v v satisfy certain conditions that encompass Molev and Sagan’s original case and conjecture positivity in the general case.

arxiv-2402-06913.title: TL;DR Progress : Multi-faceted Literature Exploration in Text Summarization
arxiv-2402-06913.creator: Shahbaz Syed † \dagger, Khalid Al-Khatib ‡ \ddagger, Martin Potthast † \dagger §, ‡ \ddagger University of Groningen, § ScaDS.AI
arxiv-2402-06913.description: Abstract This paper presents TL;DR Progress , a new tool for exploring the literature on neural text summarization. It organizes 514 papers based on a comprehensive annotation scheme for text summarization approaches and enables fine-grained, faceted search. Each paper was manually annotated to capture aspects such as evaluation metrics, quality dimensions, learning paradigms, challenges addressed, datasets, and document domains.

arxiv-2407-09522.title: UQE: A Query Engine for Unstructured Databases
arxiv-2407-09522.creator: Hanjun Dai \musEighth \musEighth, Bethany Yixin Wang \musEighth \musEighth, Xingchen Wan ‡ \ddagger, Bo Dai ¶ \lx@paragraphsign, Sherry Yang † Azade Nova † , Pengcheng Yin † , Phitchaya Mangpo Phothilimthana † , Charles Sutton † , Dale Schuurmans †§ † Google DeepMind ‡ Google Cloud § University of A
arxiv-2407-09522.description: Abstract Analytics on structured data is a mature field with many successful methods. However, most real world data exists in unstructured form, such as images and conversations. We investigate the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable unstructured data analytics.

arxiv-2601-09621.title: Diamonds in the Bulk and Large- 𝑵 N Scaling in AdS/CFT
arxiv-2601-09621.creator: Sidan A, and Tom Banks
arxiv-2601-09621.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sidan A, and Tom Banks. Quantum Field Theory (QFT) introduced us to the notion that a causal diamond in space-time corresponded to a subsystem of a quantum mechanical system defined on the global space-time. Work by Jacobson ted95 , Fischler and Susskind fs and particularly Bousso bousso ; bousso2 ; bousso3 suggested that in the quantum theory of gravity this subsystem should have a density matrix of finite entropy. These authors formalized older intuitive arguments based on black hole physics.

europmc-pmc6593152.title: Burden of disease from inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene for selected adverse health outcomes: An updated analysis with a focus on low- and middle-income countries.
europmc-pmc6593152.creator: Prüss-Ustün A, Wolf J, Bartram J, Clasen T, Cumming O, Freeman MC, Gordon B, Hunter PR, Medlicott K, Johnston R.
europmc-pmc6593152.description: Background To develop updated estimates in response to new exposure and exposure-response data of the burden of diarrhoea, respiratory infections, malnutrition, schistosomiasis, malaria, soil-transmitted helminth infections and trachoma from exposure to inadequate drinking-water

openalex-w1975146242.title: The tomato borer, Tuta absoluta, invading the Mediterranean Basin, originates from a single introduction from Central Chile
openalex-w1975146242.creator: Thomas Guillemaud, Aurélie Blin, Isabelle Le Goff, Nicolas Desneux, Maritza Reyes, Élisabeth Tabone, Anastasia Tsagkarakou, Laura Niño, Éric Lombaert
openalex-w1975146242.description: The Lepidopteran pest of tomato, Tuta absoluta, is native to South America and is invasive in the Mediterranean basin. The species' routes of invasion were investigated. The genetic variability of samples collected in South America, Europe, Africa and Middle East was analyzed...

pmc-10564404.title: Prognostic models for surgical-site infection in gastrointestinal surgery: systematic review
pmc-10564404.creator: Kenneth A McLean, Tanvi Goel, Samuel Lawday, Aya Riad, Joana Simoes, Stephen R Knight, Dhruva Ghosh, James C Glasbey, Aneel Bhangu, Ewen M Harrison, NIHR Global Health Research Unit on Global Surgery
pmc-10564404.description: BackgroundIdentification of patients at high risk of surgical-site infection may allow clinicians to target interventions and monitoring to minimize associated morbidity. The aim of this systematic review was to identify and evaluate prognostic tools for the prediction of surgical-site infection in gastrointestinal surgery.

pmc-11396851.title: A Comprehensive Review of Climate Change and Plant Diseases in Brazil
pmc-11396851.creator: Francislene Angelotti, Emília Hamada, Wagner Bettiol, Vittorio Rossi
pmc-11396851.description: Analyzing the impacts of climate change on phytosanitary problems in Brazil is crucial due to the country’s special role in global food security as one of the largest producers of essential commodities. This review focuses on the effects of climate change on plant diseases and discusses its main challenges in light of Brazil’s diverse agricultural landscape.

pmc-11434854.title: A Flowering Morphological Investigation, Fruit Fatty Acids, and Mineral Elements Dynamic Changes of Idesia polycarpa Maxim
pmc-11434854.creator: Yanpeng Wang, Cuiyu Liu, Jiasong Hu, Kaiyun Wu, Bangchu Gong, Yang Xu, Ruth Welti
pmc-11434854.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Idesia polycarpa Maxim is a high-value species of fruit oil with edible, abundant linoleic acid and polyphenols. Idesia polycarpa is described as a dioecious species, and the flowers are male; female and bisexual flowers are produced on separate plants. In order to explore the flower types of Idesia polycarpa, the morphology of its flowers and inflorescence were investigated in this study. The flower and inflorescence types, the diameter, and the flowering sequencing in male and female inflorescence were determined.

pmc-11453505.title: 6425 Impact Of Adrenalectomy On Mood, Sleep, And Quality Of Life In Patients With Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
pmc-11453505.creator: Jasmine Saini, Vanessa Fell, Beth Atkinson, Sara Achenbach, Irina Bancos
pmc-11453505.description: Disclosure: J. Saini: None. V. Fell: None. B. Atkinson: None. S. Achenbach: None. I. Bancos: None. Background: Patients with mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) have an impaired quality of life and a higher prevalence of sleep and mood disturbances as compared to patients with nonfunctioning adrenal adenomas. The impact of adrenalectomy on quality of life, mood, and sleep is unclear.

pmc-12563551.title: Iron-Based Biochar for Efficient Persulfate Activation and Sulfamethoxazole Degradation
pmc-12563551.creator: Ying Lu, Chengdu Qi, Guilong Peng, Yi Gao, Ronglong Zhang
pmc-12563551.description: In this study, we investigated the performance of iron-loaded biochar (Fe-BC) derived from mulberry branches in activating persulfate (PS) for the efficient degradation of sulfamethoxazole (SMX). The Fe-BC/PS system exhibited superior catalytic activity towards SMX degradation, achieving 97% removal within 60 min.

pmc-12636804.title: Microbial Profile and Antibiotic Sensitivity Patterns in Open Fractures: A Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Care Center
pmc-12636804.creator: Mohit Kumar, Hardik Kharbanda, Afroz Ahmed Khan, Girish Kumar Singh
pmc-12636804.description: Introduction:Open fractures are orthopedic emergencies with a high risk of infection due to soft-tissue compromise and bone exposure. Early antibiotic administration and wound debridement are critical to reducing infection-related complications. However, microbial profiles and antibiotic sensitivity patterns vary regionally, warranting local evaluation.Materials and Methods:This retrospective study was conducted over 24 months at a tertiary care center in North India.

pmc-12712478.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor Entitled “From Variant of Unknown Significance to Likely Pathogenic: Adult-Onset - Nephronophthisis Linked to NPHP4 p.T680M”
pmc-12712478.creator: Jens Christian König, Mareike Dahmer-Heath, Martin Konrad
pmc-12712478.description: um of NPHP4-associated NPH previously outlined by König et al.2 and others, while highlighting a broader point that in adults with unexplained renal insufficiency, a substantial proportion may have inherited disorders, with NPH remaining particularly underdiagnosed. NPH typically follows an insidious course, with few symptoms, gradual decline in kidney function, and largely unremarkable urinalysis.

pmc-13124010.title: Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See? Speakers Use More Redundant Color Adjectives When Speaking to Children Than Adults
pmc-13124010.creator: Maya Taliaferro, Laura Schulz
pmc-13124010.description: Cross-culturally, the evolution and production of color words has been linked to communicative efficiency. In visual search tasks for instance, speakers will direct a listener to a target by referring to both its color and shape even when all the targets are unique.

pmc-13195753.title: Untargeted metabolomic dataset of leaves from twenty-four accessions of wild and cultivated tomato plants
pmc-13195753.creator: Komla Exonam Amegan, Florent Magot, Alan Kergunteuil, Bernard Caromel, Anne-Violette Lavoir, Romain Larbat
pmc-13195753.description: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum var. lycopersicum), one of the most important crops worldwide, has a complex domestication history that began in Latin America, region hosting also fourteen wild relative species and subspecies. Domestication and subsequent breeding efforts have led to the development of the modern cultivated tomato, prized for its agronomic performance and economic value.

pmc-13239178.title: Prenatal Ultrasonographic Detection of Intracardiac Thrombi in Canine Fetuses With Congenital Heart Defects
pmc-13239178.creator: Federica Valeri, Temy Coppola, Alessandro Troisi, Riccardo Zelli, Lucia Cardinali, Elvio Lepri, Domenico Caivano, Angela Polisca
pmc-13239178.description: A 5‐year‐old pregnant Newfoundland bitch was evaluated by monitoring fetal viability. Transabdominal ultrasonography of the reproductive tract revealed a homogeneous and hyperechoic mass within the right ventricle associated with abnormal tricuspid valve in a fetus. A similar mass was also visualized in the right atrium of another fetus. The bitch delivered 11 puppies, four of which died after parturition.

pmc-13317256.title: Relationship between the advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) and all-cause and cause-specific mortality among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD): a population-based study
pmc-13317256.creator: Zhuanbo Luo, Peixu Chen, Luting Chen, Hongying Ma, Chao Cao
pmc-13317256.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is viewed as a significant health problem, and the prognosis of patients with this disease is strongly influenced by the inflammatory response and nutritional well-being of the body. The advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) provides a complete measurement of these two factors.

uslaw-usc-t19-s3702.description: United States Code, Title 19 (Customs Duties); Chapter 23 (Extension Of Certain Trade Benefits To Sub-Saharan Africa); Subchapter I (Trade Policy For Sub-Saharan Africa). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Congress supports— (1) encouraging increased trade and investment between the United States and sub-Saharan Africa; (2) reducing tariff and nontariff barriers and other obstacles to sub-Saharan African and United States trade; (3) expanding.
